coaching.headline: Every Fangtooth, both Primes, ten structures to two, and nobody ever killed Sparrow. A proper fucking mugging.
coaching.team: This was a mugging from first blood to the Core. We took every Fangtooth, both Primes and the Genesis Core, and ten structures to their two. Five of our six won exchanges were followed by an objective or structure, and they never won an exchange at all. The only weak stretch was the early offlane, where Terra kept collecting kills. Everything after that was clean and decisive.

focus.title: Bail out the bleeding lane
focus.action: When one of our laners dies twice to the same opponent before the first Fangtooth, the jungler's next gank goes to that lane.

perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's Sparrow was untouchable and lethal: nine kills, no deaths, and Ikra used as a punching bag four times, starting with first blood. That is a carry doing the fucking job; the zero is now the standard. Damage per minute ran slightly under the usual rate. When Terra is the nearest target, Sparrow shoots past to Ikra, Gideon or Grux if one is safely in range, since every basic attack into Tainted Guard cuts Sparrow's healing.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs turned the jungle into a one-sided hunting trip. Grux died to Feng Mao three times and never got a kill, while Feng Mao led the match in objective damage and the lobby in healing. After ten deaths in the last Feng Mao jungle film, one death here is the real headline. Gideon got it, so when Gideon is alive and in range before a dive, Feng Mao holds Safeguard to eat the comet or meteor first.
perPlayer.093b8010-33b3-4c96-a1ce-5b9f0515319d: BrEazy's The Fey was the engine of this stomp, and it was not close. More hero damage than anyone in the lobby, no deaths, farm well above the usual pace on the hero, and a hand in more than half our kills. Keep that standard. The next step is making Fly Trap a team call: when it grabs two or more heroes, The Fey calls it in voice so Feng Mao can drop Earth Shatter on the stunned pile.
perPlayer.6b90673a-6e08-4a75-9a19-387274cb80cb: Proper support work from KrazyKor88, and none of it needed kills to prove it. Muriel never died, our duo lost nobody early while theirs lost two, and Muriel out-warded Ikra twelve to seven. The Gideon kill came in the exchange shortly before their first tower fell. Next game, when Sparrow picks a target to shoot, Muriel throws Alacrity onto Sparrow first: the shield triggers Exarch, so those shots land faster with bonus magic damage attached. Free damage for one shield.
perPlayer.f7f51280-2487-4f54-a91d-d323df794bec: RedMxsty's Bayle played two games; the second was far better. Terra treated the early offlane like a fucking buffet: Bayle's first four deaths, three to Terra, came before anyone else on our side had died once. After the fifth, five kills and no deaths, including Grux and Ikra seconds before their inner tower dropped. Next game, after a death to the lane opponent, Bayle takes the next trade only with Dire Howl ready and stays in until its heal lands.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.matchup: Duo lane: Sparrow with Muriel into Drongo and Ikra. Ikra's Narcosis suspends the first hero it reaches and Genesis knocks up through walls; Drongo's Gag Grenade silences. Sparrow's kit has no dash, so that control was the duo threat, and it never produced a kill: neither enemy duo player killed anyone, Sparrow took first blood on Ikra, and our duo had no early deaths against two of theirs. Terra's Tainted Guard was the enemy item most relevant to an auto-attacker.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Lightning Hawk builds Momentum while moving or attacking and releases an empowered, slowing hit; Vanquisher adds penetration and executes a hero who drops very low; Tainted Rounds cuts the target's healing on basic attacks, with on-hit damage that grows as the target's health falls; Terminus adds lifesteal and turns overhealing into a shield. That is a finishing build, and Grux, the biggest healer on their side, was an obvious target for the healing cut, though the record does not show it applied. It skips the common winning Storm Breaker, Sky Splitter and Spectra core, and nothing here shows that cost anything. Final inventory does not show purchase timing.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Weald's major fires a volley of true-damage projectiles once a hero falls below a health threshold, on a per-hero cooldown; true damage ignores the armor Terra stacked. Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill, which suits a carry who farmed above the usual rate here. Wind-Rider's attack-speed burst needs a dash, leap, teleport or exit from stealth, and Heightened Senses and Pacifier are Sparrow's only triggers. Taproot is the slot-two alternative when Sparrow needs on-hit healing more than burst attack speed.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.augment: Endless Hunt resets Sparrow's basic ability cooldowns on every takedown and adds a point of physical penetration permanently each time. Nine takedowns gave it plenty to work with, though the record does not show which resets were spent. Sun Shards, ricocheting basic attacks with reduced on-hit effects, is the common alternative for wave and group damage; in a game decided by finishing targets, the reset engine fit.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.crest: Pacifier dashes, empowers the next physical hit with extra damage against low-health targets, and allows a recast after a quick kill. As Sparrow's only dash it is both the finisher and the exit, so spending it forward leaves Heightened Senses as the only way out. No deaths says the exit was never needed at the wrong time, but the feed does not record when it was cast.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.improvement: Keep the finishing package; this game of short, decisive fights gave no reason to change it. If a longer game puts Terra's armor stack in front of Sparrow for whole fights, Sky Splitter is the comparison against Terminus: damage based on the target's current health, reduced for ranged heroes, in place of the lifesteal shield. Nothing in this match tested that trade.

6b90673a-6e08-4a75-9a19-387274cb80cb.matchup: Support lane: Muriel with Sparrow into Ikra and Drongo. Ikra's Narcosis suspends the first hero it reaches and Hydroclasm bubbles slow; Drongo's Gag Grenade silences, and Grux added pulls and stuns from the jungle. Muriel's job was keeping Sparrow out of that control. Our duo had no deaths before ten minutes against two for theirs, Muriel never died, and Ikra finished with seven deaths.
6b90673a-6e08-4a75-9a19-387274cb80cb.build: Enra's Blessing shields a nearby ally who gets immobilized, a direct answer to Narcosis and Grux's stuns. Astral Catalyst shortens the ultimate cooldown on kills and assists and adds bonus damage against shielded targets. Lifecore banks charges from hero damage and fires a healing wisp at the lowest-health ally nearby; Timewarp trims non-ultimate cooldowns on a timer. The common winning core, Marshal, Crystal Tear and Windcaller, buffs allies who are nearby or being healed; this build traded that for anti-control protection and ultimate uptime.
6b90673a-6e08-4a75-9a19-387274cb80cb.eternal: Exarch makes every heal or shield grant its target bonus attack speed and magical on-hit damage for a few seconds, a natural pairing with an attack-speed carry like Sparrow. Illumination turns bonus mana regeneration into health regeneration, which Timewarp and Tranquility both feed. Fervour heals Muriel and nearby allies when Muriel basic-attacks enemy heroes. Revelation, the usual slot-one pick, shortens basic ability cooldowns on every cast instead of adding sustain.
6b90673a-6e08-4a75-9a19-387274cb80cb.augment: Sacrosanct makes Reversal of Fortune drop a Consecrated Ground at the ally's location the moment it is cast, so the shield arrives with a zone that gives allies attack speed and healing while damaging enemies inside it and cutting their attack speed. That suits a team that fought around objectives all game. The record does not show where or how often the ultimate was used.
6b90673a-6e08-4a75-9a19-387274cb80cb.crest: Tranquility's Grace heals Muriel and nearby heroes with a brief burst of damage mitigation, and Visionary grants Solstone and raises the ward cap. Muriel placed twelve wards to Ikra's seven and cleared three of the four enemy wards our team destroyed. Pacifist means diminishing gold from minion kills, which suits a support leaving the wave to Sparrow.
6b90673a-6e08-4a75-9a19-387274cb80cb.improvement: Keep the protective core into a lineup with this much control. If the next enemy team has little immobilization, Crystal Tear in place of Enra's Blessing turns every heal and shield into magical power and ability haste for both Muriel and the target, trading the anti-control shield for output. This game gave no reason to swap.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Jungle: Feng Mao into Grux, who heals through Double Pain and pulls with Smash 'n Grab. Grux finished with nine deaths, three to Feng Mao, and no kills. The gank targets that mattered were Terra, who killed Bayle four times, and Gideon, the only enemy to kill Feng Mao. Feng Mao's first two kills came on Grux and Terra in our own jungle.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Exactly the winning core. Manta Scythe hits minions and small monsters harder, adds damage against enemies with no ally nearby, and grows with camp leader and siege minion kills. Omen builds Momentum for an empowered hit that cuts non-ultimate cooldowns. The Perforator ignores part of physical armor and slows on ability damage, which has a clear target in Terra's all-armor inventory. Hero damage per minute ran about a third under Xeebs' usual Feng Mao rate, but the same items led the match in objective damage; that is a role choice, not a build fault.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Knell applies Rust on hero hits, shredding both armors up to a stack cap and handing Feng Mao part of what it shreds. Frequency adds attack speed and ability haste per Rust stack applied; Peal adds ultimate haste and applies maximum Rust for a few seconds after Earth Shatter. That loadout rewards opening with the ultimate. Fracture, the common slot-two pick, instead adds damage against targets already at maximum Rust.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Ichorous Glaive restores a slice of missing health on every unit kill and a much larger slice on an Earth Shatter execution. Feng Mao led the lobby in healing, which fits a jungler living on camp kills and executes, though the record does not split healing by source or count executions. Imperial Duelist, the more common pick, trades that sustain for a damage and damage-reduction debuff on basic-attacked targets.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Ortus grants movement speed and physical power for a short window, and takedowns inside that window add permanent power and refresh it. It is a gank and chase tool for a jungler who wants to snowball off kills. The feed does not record activations, so its share of the four kills is unknown.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: Keep the core; every Fangtooth and both Primes went our way with it. The real choice is in the Eternal at draft time: Peal suits games where Earth Shatter opens fights, while Fracture pays when fights run long enough to keep maximum Rust without the ultimate. Pick by which kind of fight the draft promises, not by this result alone.

093b8010-33b3-4c96-a1ce-5b9f0515319d.matchup: Mid: The Fey into Gideon, their highest hero-damage player, whose Black Hole drags enemies in and whose passive tether ends in a root. The Fey killed Gideon early, never died, and finished with more hero damage than anyone in the lobby. Gideon's two kills landed on Bayle and Feng Mao, not The Fey.
093b8010-33b3-4c96-a1ce-5b9f0515319d.build: Combustion adds an area burst on ability damage, recharging faster with each hero hit, and Wraith Leggings boosts ability damage to heroes below a health threshold. Caustica ignores part of magical armor and adds damage against healthy heroes carrying bonus magical armor. Spellbreaker blocks the next ability on a long cooldown, raises magical power while that shield is up, and its magical armor made The Fey the only ally itemized against Gideon. The common winning third item is Megacosm, health-based damage over time.
093b8010-33b3-4c96-a1ce-5b9f0515319d.eternal: Vesh turns part of The Fey's ability damage on heroes into an extra damage-over-time that grows with game time. Tithe of Death restores mana and adds permanent ability haste on takedowns up to a cap, and thirteen takedowns gave it plenty to feed on. Mind Rot adds current-health damage to that extra burn. This is the common default pairing, and nothing here argues against it.
093b8010-33b3-4c96-a1ce-5b9f0515319d.augment: Wild Growth gives Bramble Patch more range, so the slow and damage can be placed from further back. Range is safety for a mage, but the feed does not show placements or hits, so it cannot credit the augment for the zero deaths. Natural Infusion, stacking ability haste on Harvest Nettles hits, is the alternative for longer fights.
093b8010-33b3-4c96-a1ce-5b9f0515319d.crest: Epoch puts The Fey in stasis briefly on a long cooldown, out of reach but unable to act while it lasts. It is the answer to a committed dive such as Grux's Stampede or Terra's charge, used so the enemy spends control on nothing. The record does not show any activation.
093b8010-33b3-4c96-a1ce-5b9f0515319d.improvement: Keep Spellbreaker while a mage like Gideon is the main enemy damage; it was our only magical armor. If the next lineup has more health and less magical armor than this one, Megacosm in place of Caustica swaps magical-armor penetration for health-based damage. This match gave no reason to swap.

f7f51280-2487-4f54-a91d-d323df794bec.matchup: Offlane: Bayle into Terra. Terra built Tainted Guard, Elafrost and Gaia Greaves, all physical armor, and Tainted Guard cuts healing on any hero who basic-attacks Terra. Highland Hurl slows and shreds physical armor, and its empowered version roots instead. Terra killed Bayle four times; Bayle killed Terra once.
f7f51280-2487-4f54-a91d-d323df794bec.build: Sky Splitter deals a slice of the target's current health on each basic attack and adds lifesteal; Ashbringer shortens non-ultimate cooldowns on each basic hit, more on critical strikes; Earthshaker stacks ability damage on hero or monster hits, faster for melee heroes. That is a sustained-fighting build. Against Tainted Guard, the lifesteal and Dire Howl's omnivamp are cut while Bayle swings at Terra, so it plays best on targets like Grux and Ikra, who died to Bayle five times between them.
f7f51280-2487-4f54-a91d-d323df794bec.eternal: Weald's major fires true-damage projectiles at heroes below a health threshold, which ignores Terra's armor. Dryad's Boon shortens basic ability cooldowns on every basic hit, the same job Ashbringer does; Wind-Rider grants attack speed after a dash or leap, which Skull Crusher and Kingslayer both provide. Natural Resistance, the other slot-one option, cleanses crowd control and adds tenacity at low health, the draft alternative if roots keep ending trades.
f7f51280-2487-4f54-a91d-d323df794bec.augment: Frenzied Fighter removes Berserk's cooldown and keeps it on for as long as Bayle stays under the health threshold, so low health means attack speed, movement speed and tenacity without a timer. That rewards fighting while hurt, which is also when a root or burst finishes the trade. The record cannot show how long Bayle spent Berserk.
f7f51280-2487-4f54-a91d-d323df794bec.crest: Iceskorn Talons drops an ice sheet that gives allies on it physical power and movement speed briefly and slows enemies on it. It is a group-fight tool more than a lane-duel one. Activation is not recorded.
f7f51280-2487-4f54-a91d-d323df794bec.improvement: If Terra's sustain is what keeps winning the lane trades, Tainted Blade is the comparison against Sky Splitter: it cuts the target's healing on physical damage and adds health, giving up the current-health damage and lifesteal. Terra healed a meaningful amount here, but the record does not show when, so treat it as a test for the next Terra lane, not a proven fix.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Muriel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.winCondition: keep the carry alive with global shields and enable their damage
ourKits.passive: abilities grant Sentinel to allies; on-hit bonus
ourKits.playAgainst: she has no damage threat — dive her carry through the shields or pick her first

ourKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

ourKits.winCondition: trade with the spellshield up and execute low targets with Earth Shatter
ourKits.passive: permanent power on unique hero takedowns
ourKits.playWith: setup that holds a target for the execute
ourKits.playAgainst: bait Safeguard's spellshield before committing the key CC
